title: Redwood technical deep dive: Dedicated vs Hosted - KV cache, batching, quantization, VPC
summary: Redwood AE+SE reviewed dedicated vs hosted inference for OptiRetail. Focus on noisy neighbor/isolation, throughput guarantees, KV cache and batching strategies, quantization tradeoffs, and VPC/on-prem integration. Customer is evaluating Dedicated for predictable latency during Black Friday traffic; security and KMS were flagged as blockers. Next steps: run targeted benchmarks with customer traces, share security pack, and provide Dedicated sizing + pricing.
topics: KV cache strategy for conversational workloads
Noisy neighbor and isolation on Dedicated
action_items: Maya Patel - run 30/90/300 token p99 latency benchmark using OptiRetail sample workload and report (due 2026-06-12)
Alex Chen - send Dedicated sizing + provisional pricing and comparison spreadsheet (due 2026-06-09)
Sophie Reed - provide security questionnaire answers and clarify KMS/HSM requirements (due 2026-06-10)
next_steps: Schedule benchmark run w/ Redwood SE and OptiRetail infra (link: https://redwood.com/runbooks/dedicated-benchmark)
Share security pack and SOC2 artifact links (link: https://redwood.com/security)
Follow-up 30-min sync after benchmark to review numbers and recommended config
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), John Morales (OptiRetail Infra Lead), Lina Park (OptiRetail ML Eng), Sophie Reed (OptiRetail Security)

Summary (auto): Deep dive on Dedicated vs Hosted; benchmarking plan; action items captured.

00:00 - Alex Chen: hey everyone good afternoon thanks for joining, uh we've got Maya from our SE team and we'll dive into the technical comparisons between hosted and dedicated for your conversational use case. how's everyone doing?
00:08 - John Morales: good, thanks. quick note, we're coming off a capacity planning cycle for black friday so latency p99 during peak is the main ask.
00:16 - Maya Patel: perfect, that's what we'll focus on. quick agenda: isolation/noisy neighbor, throughput guarantees, runtime details (kv cache, batching), and quantization impacts. sound right?
00:25 - Lina Park: yep, that covers it. we also want to understand how VPC or on-prem will change the tradeoffs.
00:32 - Alex Chen: cool. quick logistics, we'll reference the deck I shared - link in chat - and we'll propose a benchmark using a slice of your production traces.

02:05 - Maya Patel: starting with isolation: hosted is multi-tenant with soft isolation, we provide limits and prioritization but under extreme peaks noisy neighbor effects can occur; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools which eliminates noisy neighbor on the serving layer. practically that means p99 variance is much tighter on Dedicated.
02:22 - John Morales: what causes the noisy neighbor mostly - scheduling, memory pressure, or kernel contention?
02:30 - Maya Patel: all of the above - GPU scheduling, PCIe bandwidth, and sometimes host-level IO. our runtime mitigates with priority lanes and prefaulting but cannot fully remove co-tenancy jitter in hosted.
02:48 - Lina Park: can you quantify? like 95/99 numbers?
02:52 - Maya Patel: ballpark for similar load: hosted p95 maybe 30-40ms but p99 can spike to 150-300ms if there are concurrent heavy jobs; Dedicated p99 tends to stay under 60-80ms for same model and requests because you get full node locality and reserved queues. we'll verify with your traces.

05:10 - Alex Chen: moving to throughput guarantees: Dedicated comes with committed throughput tiers and predictable autoscaling policies; hosted is elastic but best-effort. so if you need guaranteed qps during a sale, Dedicated is the safer choice.
05:26 - John Morales: are those guarantees SLA-backed?
05:28 - Alex Chen: yes - for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency bands tied to the capacity configuration in the contract. there are also burst policies for absorbing short spikes.

07:00 - Maya Patel: on runtime performance specifics - our engine supports continuous batching and a KV cache for chat state. KV cache reduces repeated attention work for prefixes and is very effective for multi-turn sessions. but cache hits are distribution-dependent.
07:22 - Lina Park: how is the KV cache invalidated or sharded in Dedicated vs Hosted?
07:28 - Maya Patel: in Dedicated you get local KV caches co-located with the model shard so cache hits are faster and local; in hosted the cache may be distributed with network hops depending on routing, increasing tail latency. invalidation is deterministic: we version conversation keys and expire based on token windows or explicit TTLs.

09:40 - John Morales: we do a lot of long-context sessions (2-5k tokens). does the cache save memory on the GPU or just reduce compute?
09:48 - Maya Patel: mostly reduces compute by avoiding recomputing KV for the prefix - it still uses KV cache memory (off-GPU or on-GPU depending on config) but dramatically cuts forward pass work. for very long contexts Dedicated lets you pin larger KV caches on faster local NVMe/GPU memory which helps throughput.

12:10 - Alex Chen: batching strategy - we auto-batch within a latency SLO to increase throughput. on Dedicated you can push for larger batch windows since you control node occupancy; on hosted we cap batching to avoid noisy neighbor impacts and to meet multi-tenant latency goals.
12:33 - Lina Park: do you expose batching parameters? we'd like to tune for our mix of short queries and long generations.
12:38 - Maya Patel: yes, SE can tune batching window, max batch size, and per-route priority. we usually start conservative then iterate with live traces.

15:00 - Sophie Reed: on security - VPC and KMS are critical. if we go Dedicated in our VPC, can we still use your control plane?
15:08 - Alex Chen: yes, for Redwood Private we support a private control plane with customer-managed networking, and Dedicated can be deployed in a VPC with SAML SSO, KMS integrations for key management, and audit log forwarding. for air-gapped on-prem, we offer an on-prem package but that’s a slightly different engagement.
15:28 - Sophie Reed: HSM support?
15:30 - Alex Chen: we integrate with customer KMS and HSM-backed keys where needed - we'll surface relevant docs.

17:44 - Maya Patel: quantization - we support int8 and mixed 4-bit quantization paths. quant reduces memory and increases throughput but can affect quality depending on model and prompt sensitivity. we recommend running A/B evals against your grading set.
17:59 - Lina Park: do we need to retrain or finetune after quant?
18:03 - Maya Patel: rarely; most open models work with post-training quantization. sometimes you see hallucination regressions at edge cases; that's why we tie quality monitoring to prompt/eval sets before rolling quantized configs to production.

20:20 - John Morales: for our recommendation engine (short completions) we prioritize throughput. quant seems attractive. for chat use-cases with long context we'd be more cautious.
20:32 - Maya Patel: exactly - quantize stateless completion models more aggressively. for chat with heavy KV reliance, pinning a higher-fidelity model on Dedicated for that route is a common pattern.

23:10 - Alex Chen: about tail latency and autoscale - Dedicated nodes let us maintain steady queueing behavior; hosted autoscale is faster for bursty unpredictable traffic but without throughput guarantees. tradeoff: hosted lowers ops and cost but Dedicated gives predictability and isolation.
23:36 - John Morales: curious about cost delta - rough percent?
23:40 - Alex Chen: rough ballpark 20-50% premium for Dedicated depending on commit and GPU type, but when you factor in reduced error budgets and conversion impact during peak events, Dedicated often pays back for high-value users. we'll include numbers in the sizing spreadsheet.

26:00 - Lina Park: workload placement - can we route certain routes to Dedicated and fall back to hosted?
26:06 - Maya Patel: yes - smart routing policies let you pin routes to Dedicated and set fallback chains to hosted variants; that hybrid helps manage cost while keeping critical paths isolated.

28:50 - Sophie Reed: network egress and data residency - going Dedicated in our region helps keep data within required boundaries?
28:58 - Alex Chen: yes we deploy Dedicated in specified regions and can ensure data residency. for Private on-prem it's fully controlled by you.

31:10 - Maya Patel: benchmark plan proposal: we'll run three scenarios using your traces: 1) conversational multimodal-like (2-5k tokens), 2) short completions (30-200 tokens) high qps, 3) mixed. measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU util, and cache hit rates.
31:32 - John Morales: that sounds good. what's the expected runtime?
31:36 - Maya Patel: each scenario ~2 hours to ramp and gather stable stats; we'll share the scripts and metrics dashboard.

34:00 - Lina Park: question on KV cache warmup - how do you handle cold-starts when traffic hits a new shard?
34:06 - Maya Patel: we pre-warm popular prefixes using a small write-behind cache and heuristics. for Dedicated you can persist cache across restarts more reliably. cold starts still impact tail, which is why warmup is part of the benchmark.

36:40 - John Morales: any pitfalls for on-prem? we have limited rack-space and NVLink topology concerns.
36:47 - Maya Patel: on-prem requires coordination on topology; our on-prem package has a preflight checklist for NVLink, GPU types, and network fabric. if you lack NVLink we adjust sharding to avoid cross-host attention overheads but throughput will differ.

39:10 - Alex Chen: operational controls - Redwood Console gives per-route token costs, latency histograms, and tracing. for Dedicated we'll grant your ops team RBAC and audit log forwarding to your SIEM.
39:28 - Sophie Reed: can we pull exportable trace logs for PD and SRE?
39:31 - Maya Patel: yes, logs and spans are exportable to e.g., Datadog/Tempo or S3 buckets.

42:00 - John Morales: if we start with Hosted to validate functionality and then move to Dedicated for Black Friday, what's the typical migration effort?
42:07 - Alex Chen: migration is mostly a config and routing change - you can pin model versions and switch to Dedicated when ready. effort is usually a few sprints for integrations and testing, depending on VPC and compliance chores.

45:20 - Lina Park: testers - can you run a canary on a small portion of traffic to measure regression after quantization?
45:27 - Maya Patel: yes, rollouts support canaries and automatic fallback if quality drops. we also have evaluation harnesses to run prompt suites against both variants.

48:00 - Alex Chen: time check - we're at about 48 minutes - last block: cost optimization strategies on Dedicated - batching, cache pinning, model mix (smaller models for low-critical routes), and autoscaling policies.
48:20 - John Morales: for our estimated 5k concurrent users at peak, what Dedicated footprint do you recommend?
48:28 - Maya Patel: ballpark we'd start recommending a 4-node A100 pool with autoscale buffer depending on QPS profile; we'll size precisely after the benchmark.

51:10 - Sophie Reed: compliance question - do you provide SOC2 reports when Dedicated is in our VPC?
51:17 - Alex Chen: yes, Redwood provides SOC2 Type II artifacts and third-party audit evidence; some on-prem deployments require additional local attestations which we can discuss.

54:30 - Maya Patel: practical constraints: if you have strict HSM-only encryption for tokens, that can add latency to per-request crypto ops. we usually colocate crypto endpoints or use local KMS proxies to reduce latency.
54:50 - Sophie Reed: good to know. we'll share our KMS requirements in the questionnaire.

57:00 - Alex Chen: recap - Redwood will: 1) schedule benchmark with sample traces, 2) run three scenarios and share dashboards, 3) deliver Dedicated sizing + provisional pricing, 4) share security pack and SOC2 links.
57:18 - John Morales: sounds good. can you get the benchmark scheduled by next week?
57:22 - Maya Patel: yes - proposing 2026-06-09 or 06-10 for the bench run, we'll confirm in email.

59:50 - Lina Park: last quick one - any gotchas on third-party libs or custom ops? we have a few custom tokenizers and a small LLM finetune.
59:58 - Maya Patel: custom tokenizers typically are fine; for custom ops we need to validate CUDA kernel compatibility on Dedicated nodes during preflight. we'll surface the checklist.

61:30 - Alex Chen: thanks everyone - we'll follow up with artifacts and calendar invites. appreciate the time.
61:36 - John Morales: thanks, talk soon.
61:40 - Sophie Reed: thanks all.

Links referenced: https://redwood.com/decks/dedicated-vs-hosted.pdf | https://redwood.com/runbooks/dedicated-benchmark | https://redwood.com/security
